guidelines.detail: same as LRN-019 (The description says IT assesses the request by checking compatibility, cost and resource needs, with no order among the checks, before the approval decision. The generated model collapsed these into one task, and the reference has a parallel gateway pair around the assessment tasks (M8, M10) and a separate compatibility task (M1). The documented guideline GW-04 only covers parallel splits in gene)

same as LRN-004 (The reference starts with a plain start event followed by a submission task (M12, M2). The generated model has a start event labeled 'IT solution request received' (X1) and no submission task, so the submitting action is missing as a task. LRN-004 already requires a separate task for the party's action after the start event, so this is the same guideline applied to the start; the gap comes from no)

refines ACT-04 (The reference models the stated submission as a start event followed by a task that leads into the assessment. The generated model used a sendTask for the submission, added a separate start event for the received request, and added an end event after the submission. The description states no message being sent, so the sendTask is a wrong choice of element type. The extra start and end events break)

refines ACT-04 (M1 shows the reference has a task for the submission before the parallel 'Start assessment' gateway, while X2 shows the generated model used a sendTask for the same step. S1 describes the submission as a participant's action that triggers the process. X4 shows a separate start event was added for the same step. rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description lists two or more activities that follow one step or act on the same item, and it states no order among them, only that they are performed to be completed before a later step: Model these activities as the outgoing branches of a parallel gateway that opens them all, and close them with a parallel gateway that joins all branches before the next step that depends on their completion. Do not sequence them one after another and do not add decision conditions to these branches.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that one submitted item is evaluated through several distinct checks, with no order stated between them, and all of them must be completed before a decision is made on that item

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says the process starts when a party (such as a department) performs a stated action, for example identifying a need, before any further work is described: Model a start event for the triggering occurrence, and place a separate task directly after it that is named with the action the party performs. Do not fold that action into the start event's label. Connect the task to the next step of the described flow.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says the process starts when a party (such as an employee or department) submits a request, and the submission is the stated first action before any further work is described

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says the process starts when a party performs a stated action (for example, submitting something) and names no message, signal, or other message exchange that the action sends: Model the process start as a bpmn:startEvent with no incoming sequence flow. Place a plain bpmn:task (not a bpmn:sendTask) for the party's action directly after the start event, and connect it by a sequence flow to the next step of the described flow. Do not add a second start event for the action, and do not add an end event after the action.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says the process starts when a party performs a stated action (for example, submitting something) and names no message, signal, or other message exchange that the action sends

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says a participant submits or raises a request that starts the process, as an action the participant performs (for example filling in and submitting a request), not as a message the process sends to another system or party: Model that submission as a plain bpmn:task (performed work) that comes after the single process start event and before the parallel split into the assessment branches. Do not model it as a bpmn:sendTask, and do not give it its own start or end event.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says a participant submits or raises a request that starts the process, as an action the participant performs (for example filling in and submitting a request), not as a message the process sends to another system or party
